_note: The map behind the door in the western wall, and the first one drawn at a different scale. West Bambulon is twenty tiles of walking; this is sixteen tiles of country, and one of them is West Bambulon. So the terrain vocabulary is its own — plain, coast, range, sea — and a range is not a cliff you walk round in an afternoon. **`sea` is not `water`**: `Rule::Wade` opens the rim of anything drawn `~`, and an ocean drawn with it would be an ocean the Toad set walks the edge of. Three regions, banded south to north, and the band the door opens onto is rated where West Bambulon's hardest one leaves off — a player who has beaten the Cave arrives at level twelve or better, so bracketing this at five to nine would have put a whole continent below the map it opens off. Two places are written as events rather than gates because the maps they promise are not built yet: a road that says where it goes is a promise, and a gate onto a map this build has not got is a hole.

places.name: the road west to Kettleworks
prose: The road west stops being a road eleven times and starts again eleven times, and the eleventh time it starts it is cobbled and swept and somebody has been sweeping it.
There is a field at the end of it with a town at one corner and a thing in the middle you take for a hill until you are four miles closer.

places.name: the edge of the Wextreen Reach
places.shut: The plain stops being the sort of ground that has a next tile, and what is past it will not hold a footprint. Nine people have surveyed it and none of them agreed; you have nothing to read it with and it has nothing to say.
prose: Whatever you are carrying settles, and the edge stops being an edge — not by moving, but by acquiring a far side.
It is a field. It has hedges in it and a lane and a stone pillar in the middle with a brass plate on top, and nine cairns where nine people stopped.
